finalOutput:
I created `snake_anthropic-claude-haiku-5-5_01.html` in the project root as a single self-contained file (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript). I did not run it in a browser, so it is checked only by reading the generated code.

**What's in it**
- **Board:** a 30x30 grid drawn on a canvas, with 20px cells.
- **Movement:** the snake moves continuously every 100 ms in one of four directions. Reversing directly is blocked, and a short input queue keeps quick key presses from being lost.
- **Growth and death:** eating food adds a segment and one point. Hitting a wall or the snake's own body ends the round.
- **Controls:**
  - Player 1 uses W A S D.
  - Player 2 uses the arrow keys.
  - In CPU vs Human, the human can use either set.
  - P pauses and resumes.
- **CPU mode:** the CPU snake finds the shortest safe path to food with breadth-first search. If no safe path exists, it picks the move that leaves the most reachable space.
- **Game modes:** Human vs Human, CPU vs Human, and CPU vs CPU. Each is selected from the start menu with the mouse, the arrow keys plus Enter, or keys 1/2/3.
- **Round end:**
  - Human vs Human ends when either snake dies.
  - CPU vs Human ends when the human's snake dies.
  - CPU vs CPU ends when both snakes have died.
  - The round also ends if the board fills with no food left.
- **HUD:** the current mode and each snake's score are shown above the board during play.
- **Game over screen:** shows the winner or a draw, plus final scores. Press Enter or R to restart the same mode, or Space, Escape, or M to return to the menu.

**Things to check when you open it**
- The CPU is simple and can still trap itself in long games.
- In CPU vs CPU, both snakes can die in the same tick; the code then counts it as a draw or decides by score.

- Canvas-based game board: a 30x30 grid of square cells (e.g. 20px per cell = 600x600 canvas), centered on the page with a dark background, a score panel above the board showing "Player 1 / Player 2" scores as applicable and the current mode name.
- Snake moves continuously on a timer (tick about every 100ms) in one of four directions (up, down, left, right). Snake grows by one segment when it eats food; food is placed at a random empty cell (never on a snake). Prevent immediate 180-degree reversal (direction changes are applied per tick, queued so that a reversal into the neck is ignored).
- Collision with a wall or with the snake's own body ends the game for that snake. Hitting a wall or itself ends the game (for the round in CPU vs CPU / human-vs-CPU modes, a snake that dies is marked dead; the round ends when the human snake dies, or when all snakes are dead in cpu vs cpu; in human vs human the round ends when either snake dies, or in both-dead case the higher score wins).
- Game modes, selected from a start menu: (1) Human vs Human: two human players. Player 1 (blue/green snake) uses Arrow keys? NO — Player 1 uses W/A/S/D, Player 2 uses Arrow keys. (2) CPU vs Human: Player 1 is human (W/A/S/D or arrow keys), CPU snake is the second snake. (3) CPU vs CPU: both snakes are controlled by the CPU.
- CPU AI: each tick, the CPU snake computes a BFS shortest path from its head to the food over empty cells (treating both snakes' bodies and walls as obstacles, excluding the tail cell which will move away). If a path exists it takes the first step; if no path exists, it picks any safe move that does not immediately collide, preferring the move that keeps the most reachable free space (flood-fill count). Avoid moving into obstacles.
- Keyboard controls: W/A/S/D and Arrow keys mapped per mode as described. Keys must call preventDefault for arrows/space to avoid page scroll.
- Score display during gameplay: current score for each snake shown on screen (e.g. "P1: 5   CPU: 3") and the mode name.
- Start menu overlay: title "SNAKE", three mode buttons (Human vs Human, CPU vs Human, CPU vs CPU) that can be clicked AND selected with keys 1/2/3 or arrow up/down + Enter. Show control hints.
- Game over screen overlay: shows the winner / result text and final scores, and the message "Press ENTER or R to restart" / "Press SPACE to return to menu" style prompt. Restart is allowed with a keypress (Enter or R restarts the same mode; Escape or M returns to the menu).
- Pause with P key during gameplay (optional but nice).
- Use requestAnimationFrame or setInterval-based game loop; ensure no double timers when restarting (clear existing interval).
- Clean, commented, well-structured code with camelCase names for functions and methods. Code in English.
- Output the complete final file; do not truncate."}
